review_scope: Exact 2f0a40c fresh analyses. All 26 complete original results, resolved rules, primary finding sources and 57 supporting sources remain identical to the previously reviewed 33a6d5d context. source_review: Reviewed all eight changed business files. Checkpoint compatibility adds a v10 transition only for the established unaffected provider/draft stages while retaining strict equality of all non-rule fields. Saved schedules are revalidated, expired checkpoints and route observations are not renewed.

The scheduler marks unsent budget-deferred route lookups and excludes them from persisted attempted-route checkpoints. Previously attempted failures remain unverified and are not automatically retried; no new endpoint, credential source, process execution, permission or network destination is introduced.

Quantity adjustments and summary rebuilding operate on the final selected POI list, produce typed JSON data and nonblocking quality issues, and preserve out-of-scope days. They do not add raw HTML rendering, source authorization changes, deserialization capabilities or access to hidden user data.
Result.vue displays numeric adjustment counts through Vue property bindings and fixed explanatory text. It introduces no v-html, URL, script or event-handler string construction from external input.

The new regression tests and browser scenario cover visible count warnings, final-attraction summaries and default-budget resume. These changes do not alter the previously assessed custom CSRF guard, compare-and-swap arithmetic, validation-only routes, fixture credential boundaries, public package download permissions or embedded Chroma execution mode.

Compared each complete original SARIF result and resolved rule descriptor, primary source bytes, ordered semantic-flow hash and all supporting sources. No additional or changed raw finding was found. No directory-wide, query-wide or severity-wide suppression is added.

findings.explanation: Current SecurityConfiguration validates X-CSRF-Token against BrowserSession.csrf(token) on cookie-authenticated non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests before token authentication and handler dispatch. Missing/mismatched tokens return403. Explicit Bearer credentials are not ambient browser credentials. Public login/register/recovery/email capability routes do not inherit cookie authentication; email reset consumes its secret capability and still enforces enabled MFA. Browser cookies remain host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, and Secure outside loopback. Disabling Spring built-in CSRF is not the absence of the bound custom guard.
limitations: Scope is the current filter ordering, exact credential endpoints, cookie configuration and actual handlers. Changing any requires reassessment.
Safe-read map request accounting is separately assessed in codeql-csrf-review.json; this is not a claim that every GET has no database side effect.

findings.explanation: The request int version reaches Java +1 only after a matching parameterized PostgreSQL INTEGER update SET version=version+1 returns affected rows1. A mismatch throws409, and a matching INT_MAX overflows in PostgreSQL before Java can execute +1. Existing stored versions start at1 and no current production assignment injects arbitrary versions. The largest successful Java operand is2147483646 and result2147483647. The controller/service order, SQL predicate/rowcount check and INTEGER schema were read in current source; the full fresh source-to-sink traces were also read.
limitations: Finite PostgreSQL INTEGER version exhaustion can reject the next update; successful infinite version growth or absence of a500 at that boundary is not claimed.
Changing version type, assignment sources, SQL predicate, rowcount guard or moving arithmetic before the update requires reassessment.

findings.explanation: Both ordered flow steps and all related locations read. The reported source is SecureRandom.nextBytes(nonce) at line70, flowing to nonce.length. Local nonce is allocated new byte[12]; nextBytes fills elements and cannot change Java array length. The second operand value.length was independently audited rather than ignored.
limitations: There is no application-level numeric maximum for trusted PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Therefore this review does not claim a fixed absolute allocation maximum across all possible operator configurations. The symbolic bound and sufficient threshold are explicit; runtime memory size or low probability is not used as a justification.

The finding is not exploitable through current remote inputs: the only remote payload component is bounded email; the reported nonce-length input is constant. This decision is scoped to the enumerated current call graph and deployment-config trust boundary, not a general safe-for-arbitrary-text claim about encrypt/enqueue.
New enqueue callers, user-editable base URLs, changed templates, recipient schema, serializer settings, nonce/GCM settings or origin trust require new source-and-trace review.

findings.explanation: The reported nonce is allocated new byte[12]; SecureRandom fills its elements without changing length. Current production Totp.encrypt callers pass the32-character base32 result of20 server-generated random bytes. AES-GCM adds16 tag bytes; the final allocation is12+32+16=60 bytes. All Totp.encrypt/decrypt call sites in current AccountSecurityService were inspected. New SMTP encryption uses its separate MailDeliveryService.encrypt method, and is not silently included in this fixed-TOTP bound.
limitations: The public Totp helper could be called with arbitrary strings by future Java code. This review binds the current complete call graph, not a general arbitrary-input guarantee.

findings.explanation: The complete fresh flow was read together with the current prepare implementation. Actual synthetic username/password/TOTP seed are written to the explicitly ignored local credential file; prepare returns only readiness/MFA booleans, a status integer, next-login epoch and a literal credential-location note. The main print serializes that status result, not credentials. prepare also verifies permitted project, validation flags, candidate label where applicable and a real offline fixture marker before account creation.
limitations: The ignored credential file remains sensitive; this is not permission to publish it or log arbitrary future prepare response fields.
Caller/return-shape, fixture guards and the credential-file location are part of the exact bound context.

findings.explanation: The complete fresh flow is the0755 chmod of a newly created build-only TemporaryDirectory. Its contents are public signed Debian package archives downloaded from the pinned package lock, verified by package identity/architecture/SHA256 and SONAME before install. The script requires POSIX root plus the explicit Docker-build flag. No account, SMTP, API credential or private runtime/config file is written into this directory.0755 lets the package-download sandbox traverse public build artifacts; it is not a secret-file permission.
limitations: 0755 is not approved for secret files/directories or other chmod sites. Directory contents, build guard and package-verification flow are bound.

findings.explanation: The complete fresh flows terminate in the owner/editor username templates. Math.random contributes uniqueness to public synthetic account identifiers and the test idempotency suffix; it does not generate the fixed fixture password, server session, CSRF capability or cryptographic key. Playwright loads e2e explicitly. The application entry is /src/main.ts, tsconfig includes src only, and the final frontend image serves only Vite dist; this test module is not product runtime entropy.
limitations: The old operations test allows E2E_BASE_URL override and has no positive fixture marker check. Use the authorized isolated validation target; this finding review is not approval to run fixture accounts/passwords on arbitrary production targets.
Do not reuse Math.random for production credentials, session tokens, recovery capabilities or security entropy.

findings.explanation: Both complete fresh flows are Math.random -> base36 -> slice -> public_${Date.now()}_${suffix}. The value becomes a public test username and @example.test inbox recipient. The test password is a separate fixed fixture literal; verification/reset tokens are read from real isolated Mailpit and are generated by the backend SecureRandom, not this value. The module imports Playwright and is outside the src-only application build graph. The test is skipped unless dedicated base/inbox variables exist, but that is configuration context, not proof arbitrary supplied targets are safe.
limitations: The offline browser boundary only restricts browser subresources to the selected origin; it does not authenticate that operator-selected PUBLIC_E2E_BASE_URL or TEST_MAILPIT_URL is a fixture. CI/dedicated validation configuration supplies those isolated services.
The fixed password is a test fixture and not a product credential. No claim permits this pattern for production secrets.
